reasons: Redline is directionally correct for us as customer: it adds the USD 2M CGL aggregate, raises E&O from USD 1M to USD 2M, and adds USD 5M cyber/privacy liability, reaching the preferred position without weakening any existing protection.

Edit is surgical and grammatical — workers' compensation, certificates-on-request and notice-of-material-change language are untouched, and the existing sentence structure is preserved; the 0.427 changed-character ratio reflects the necessary limit insertions rather than an unnecessary rewrite.

Reclassifying from the planner's 'missing' hint to a deviation is correct on the cited text: Section 14 (p0048) does contain an insurance obligation, so amending limits in place is the smaller edit than inserting a duplicate paragraph.

Comment is accurate and consistent with the redline (identifies the covered elements, the three gaps, and the data/systems access trigger for cyber cover) and offers the documented fallback of USD 2M cyber with E&O at USD 1M in the prescribed concise, first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.
Omission of the model language's one-year tail is acceptable since the stated preferred position does not require it and the drafter flagged the choice as a minimality trade-off.
